Implement the Rectifications feature for the Lift Servicing Digitisation app.
This is an individual feature (owner: Ryan) 

Reuse the existing shared
useFileUpload hook and the /api/uploads/presign route for all file uploads
(photos and signature) — do not build a separate upload path.

WORKFLOW THIS FEATURE SUPPORTS
After a defect is fixed, the EM services staff and the lift company do a
joint on-site inspection. The lift company then submits proof of the fix
(photos) and e-signs to confirm the work is done. The rectification record
then shows on the Rectifications page with the photos and signature visible,
so EM staff can review and endorse it.

DATA MODEL — server/models/Rectification.js
- defectId (ObjectId, ref: Defect, required) — the defect this rectifies
- rectifiedBy (String, required) — name of the lift company technician
- liftCompanyName (String)
- dateRectified (Date, required)
- proofPhotos (Array of String) — S3 URLs, at least 1 required before
  submission, allow multiple
- signatureUrl (String, required) — S3 URL of the e-signature image
- remarks (String, optional)
- status (String, enum: ["Draft", "Submitted", "Endorsed"], default: "Draft")
- endorsedBy (String, optional) — filled in when EM staff endorses after
  the joint inspection
- endorsedDate (Date, optional)
- isDeleted (Boolean, default: false) — soft delete, only allowed while
  status is "Draft"
- timestamps: true

BACKEND — server/routes/rectifications.js + controllers/rectificationController.js
Standard CRUD, plus one extra action:
- GET /api/rectifications — list all (excluding soft-deleted), populate
  defectId with basic defect info (description, liftId) for display
- GET /api/rectifications/:id — single record, fully populated
- POST /api/rectifications — create as "Draft" or "Submitted" depending on
  whether photos + signature are present; validate at least 1 photo and a
  signatureUrl are provided before allowing status "Submitted"
- PUT /api/rectifications/:id — update fields; if status is "Endorsed",
  block edits to proofPhotos/signatureUrl (record is finalized) but still
  allow remarks
- PATCH /api/rectifications/:id/endorse — separate endpoint for EM staff
  to mark status "Endorsed", sets endorsedBy + endorsedDate; only allowed
  if status is currently "Submitted"
- DELETE /api/rectifications/:id — soft delete; return 400 if status is
  not "Draft" (can't delete a submitted/endorsed record)
- Proper error handling: 404 if not found, 400 for validation errors,
  meaningful error messages in the response body

FRONTEND — client/src/features/rectifications/
- RectificationsSection.jsx — the section shown when the Rectifications
  tab is active
  - Table/list of rectification records: defect description, lift company,
    date rectified, status badge (Draft/Submitted/Endorsed), thumbnail of
    first photo
  - Click a row to open RectificationDetail.jsx (or an expandable panel)
    showing: full photo gallery (all proofPhotos, click to enlarge), the
    signature image, remarks, and endorsement info if endorsed
  - "New Rectification" button opens RectificationForm.jsx
- RectificationForm.jsx — create/edit form
  - Dropdown/search to select the defect being rectified (fetch from
    GET /api/defects for the picker — read-only cross-feature call, do not
    duplicate defect CRUD logic here)
  - rectifiedBy, liftCompanyName, dateRectified fields
  - Photo upload: multiple file input, each file goes through
    useFileUpload.js, show upload progress and thumbnail previews,
    allow removing a photo before submit
  - E-signature: signature pad component (use react-signature-canvas or
    a simple <canvas> with pointer events if you want zero extra deps) —
    let the lift company draw their signature, "Clear" button to redo it,
    on submit convert the canvas to a PNG blob and upload it through
    useFileUpload.js just like a photo, store the returned URL as
    signatureUrl
  - Save as Draft vs Submit — Submit requires at least 1 photo + signature
  - Edit mode: pre-fill all fields, disable photo/signature editing if
    status is already "Endorsed"
- EndorseButton.jsx — small component shown only to EM staff role (or
  just always visible for now if you haven't built auth/roles yet) on a
  "Submitted" record, calls PATCH /api/rectifications/:id/endorse,
  prompts for endorsedBy name
- useRectifications.js — hook wrapping all the fetch calls above
  (list, get one, create, update, endorse, delete)

TESTS
- backend/tests/ryan/test-cases.md listing test cases for the rectification
  controller (e.g. "cannot delete a Submitted record", "cannot endorse a
  Draft record", "create requires defectId")
- backend/tests/ryan/rectification.test.js — unit tests for the controller
  logic above (mock the DB or use an in-memory MongoDB for tests)
- frontend/tests/ryan/test-cases.md listing test cases for the UI
  (e.g. "submit button disabled until signature is drawn", "shows all
  uploaded photos in gallery")
- frontend/tests/ryan/RectificationForm.test.jsx — basic component tests

DELIVERABLE
Working end-to-end: creating a rectification record with real photo
uploads and a drawn signature, viewing it with photos + signature
displayed, and endorsing it.

1	const mongoose = require('mongoose');
2	
3	// Severity matches the terminology already used for embedded defects on inspection
4	// reports (see models/inspections/Inspection.js) for consistency across the app.
5	const DEFECT_SEVERITIES = ['Minor', 'Major', 'Critical'];
6	
7	// A standalone defect has its own lifecycle, separate from the lightweight
8	// Open/Acknowledged/Verified status used for defects embedded on an inspection report.
9	const DEFECT_STATUSES = ['Open', 'In Progress', 'Resolved', 'Closed'];
10	
11	const defectSchema = new mongoose.Schema(
12	  {
13	    // Assigned by the controller from the current max in the collection (see
14	    // nextDefectNo in defectController.js), not an ever-incrementing counter -
15	    // mirrors reportNo in models/inspections/Inspection.js so deleting the
16	    // highest-numbered defect and creating a new one reissues that number
17	    // instead of skipping ahead.
18	    defectNo: { type: String, required: true, unique: true, trim: true },
19	
20	    title: { type: String, required: true, trim: true },
21	    description: { type: String, default: '', trim: true },
22	
23	    // Optional link to a real lift asset. Not required, since a defect can be
24	    // logged against a general area (e.g. "Blk 12 lift lobby") before anyone
25	    // has pinned down exactly which lift is at fault. liftCode/block are a
26	    // snapshot taken at creation time (see resolveLiftSnapshot in the
27	    // controller) - a defect is a historical record and shouldn't silently
28	    // change if the lift's block gets reassigned later.
29	    liftId: { type: mongoose.Schema.Types.ObjectId, ref: 'Lift', default: null },
30	    liftCode: { type: String, default: '', trim: true },
31	    location: { type: String, required: true, trim: true },
32	
33	    severity: { type: String, enum: DEFECT_SEVERITIES, required: true },
34	    status: { type: String, enum: DEFECT_STATUSES, default: 'Open' },
35	
36	    reportedBy: { type: String, default: 'Unknown', trim: true },
37	    reportedDate: { type: Date, default: Date.now },
38	
39	    // Set by the controller the moment status first reaches Resolved - kept even if
40	    // later reopened, so "how long did this take to fix" stays answerable.
41	    resolvedDate: { type: Date, default: null },
42	  },
43	  { timestamps: true }
44	);
45	
46	module.exports = mongoose.model('Defect', defectSchema);
47	module.exports.DEFECT_SEVERITIES = DEFECT_SEVERITIES;
48	module.exports.DEFECT_STATUSES = DEFECT_STATUSES;

Feature owner: Ryan
Automated in: `rectification.test.js` (Jest + Supertest, against an in-memory MongoDB via

| 6 | Create — explicit `status: "Submitted"` without proof | POST with `status: "Submitted"` but no photos/signature | 400; message mentions both "at least 1 proof photo" and "a signature" |
| 7 | Create — explicit `status: "Submitted"` missing only the signature | POST with photos but no `signatureUrl`, `status: "Submitted"` | 400; message mentions "a signature" only |
| 8 | List — excludes soft-deleted records | Create two records, soft-delete one via DELETE, GET `/api/rectifications` | 200; only the non-deleted record is returned |
| 9 | List — populates defect summary | Create a record against a real defect, GET the list | 200; `defectId` in the response is an object with `defectNo`/`title`/`description`/`liftId` rather than a bare id string |
| 10 | Get one — unknown id | GET a well-formed but non-existent id | 404 |
| 11 | Get one — fully populated | GET an existing record's id | 200; `defectId` is populated |
| 12 | Update — can't submit without proof | PUT `status: "Submitted"` on a Draft record with no photos/signature | 400 |
| 13 | Update — can reach Submitted once proof is attached | PUT `proofPhotos` + `signatureUrl` + `status: "Submitted"` in one request | 200; `status` is `"Submitted"` |
| 14 | Update — can't set status directly to Endorsed | PUT `status: "Endorsed"` on a Submitted record | 400; message points at the endorse endpoint |
| 15 | Update — blocks photo/signature edits once Endorsed | Endorse a record, then PUT a new `proofPhotos` array | 400 |
| 16 | Update — still allows remarks once Endorsed | Endorse a record, then PUT a new `remarks` value | 200; `remarks` updates, `proofPhotos`/`signatureUrl` untouched |
| 17 | Update — unknown id | PUT a well-formed but non-existent id | 404 |
| 18 | Endorse — cannot endorse a Draft record | PATCH `/:id/endorse` on a freshly-created Draft record | 400; message says it must be "Submitted" first |
| 19 | Endorse — requires `endorsedBy` | PATCH `/:id/endorse` on a Submitted record with an empty body | 400 |
| 20 | Endorse — happy path | PATCH `/:id/endorse` with `endorsedBy` on a Submitted record | 200; `status` is `"Endorsed"`, `endorsedBy` matches, `endorsedDate` is set |
| 21 | Endorse — cannot endorse twice | Endorse a record, then PATCH `/:id/endorse` again | 400; message says it must be "Submitted" first |
| 22 | Delete — cannot delete a Submitted record | Submit a record, then DELETE it | 400; only Draft records can be deleted |
| 23 | Delete — cannot delete an Endorsed record | Endorse a record, then DELETE it | 400 |
| 24 | Delete — happy path on a Draft record | DELETE a freshly-created Draft record, then GET the same id | DELETE 200; subsequent GET 404 (soft-deleted, not just hidden) |
| 25 | Delete — unknown id | DELETE a well-formed but non-existent id | 404 |

## Manual / exploratory checks (not automated)

| # | Test case | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 26 | Upload real photos and a drawn signature through the UI, then Submit | `POST /api/uploads/presign` is called once per file, each S3 URL lands in `proofPhotos`/`signatureUrl`, and the record shows as "Submitted" in the table |
| 27 | Open a Submitted record as EM staff and click Endorse | Prompted for an endorser name; after confirming, the record shows "Endorsed" with that name and today's date |
| 28 | Try to edit photos on an Endorsed record in the UI | Photo upload/remove controls and the signature pad are disabled; remarks stays editable |

## Media Storage

File uploads (photos, e-signatures, etc.) go through [Cloudinary](https://cloudinary.com)
via a signed-upload flow: the backend hands out a short-lived signature
(`POST /api/uploads/signature`), and the frontend uploads the file straight to Cloudinary
with it - file bytes never pass through our server, and `CLOUDINARY_API_SECRET` never
reaches the browser.

To set this up locally (or in a deployed environment):
1. Create a free account at [cloudinary.com](https://cloudinary.com/users/register/free).
2. On the dashboard home page, find your **Cloud name**, **API Key**, and **API Secret**
   under "Account Details" / "API Keys".
3. Copy those three values into `backend/.env`:
   ```
   CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME=your-cloud-name
   CLOUDINARY_API_KEY=your-api-key
   CLOUDINARY_API_SECRET=your-api-secret
   ```
4. No frontend env vars are needed for this - the frontend only ever talks to our own
   backend for the signature, then to Cloudinary directly using the (non-secret) cloud
   name and API key that endpoint returns.

Any feature can reuse the shared `useFileUpload` hook (`frontend/src/hooks/useFileUpload.js`)
to upload a file: `const { uploadFile, uploading, progress } = useFileUpload();` then
`const url = await uploadFile(file, 'your-feature-folder')` - the optional `folder` argument
just organizes uploads by feature in the Cloudinary dashboard (e.g. `"rectifications"`).

Cloudinary migration is complete and verified end-to-end. Summary:

**Backend**
- [backend/src/utils/cloudinary.js](em-services-lift-servicing/backend/src/utils/cloudinary.js) (new) — configures the `cloudinary` SDK from `CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME/API_KEY/API_SECRET`; safe to import with no env vars set (no network call at config time).
- [backend/src/routes/uploads.js](em-services-lift-servicing/backend/src/routes/uploads.js) — S3 presign logic replaced with `POST /api/uploads/signature`, which signs `{timestamp, folder?}` via `cloudinary.utils.api_sign_request` and returns `{signature, timestamp, apiKey, cloudName, folder}`. The API secret never leaves the server. 503s if Cloudinary env vars aren't set yet.
- [server.js](em-services-lift-servicing/backend/src/server.js) comment updated to reflect Cloudinary instead of S3.
- `@aws-sdk/client-s3` and `@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner` removed from `package.json`/node_modules (26 packages gone); `cloudinary` added and installed.

**Frontend**
- [frontend/src/hooks/useFileUpload.js](em-services-lift-servicing/frontend/src/hooks/useFileUpload.js) — rewritten to call `/api/uploads/signature`, then POST a `FormData` straight to `https://api.cloudinary.com/v1_1/<cloudName>/auto/upload`, returning `secure_url`. Signature kept **backward-compatible**: `uploadFile(file, folder?)`, same `{uploadFile, uploading, progress, error}` return shape — so Scheduling's `ScheduleFormDialog.jsx` (Aeric's feature) keeps working with zero changes, verified by rerunning `test:aeric`.
- My Rectifications photo/signature uploads now pass `folder: 'rectifications'` for dashboard organization.

**Docs/config**
- `backend/.env.example`: AWS vars swapped for `CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME/API_KEY/API_SECRET`.
